description: Closed ontology for literature knowledge-graph extraction (bundle B, semantic governance). Any entity type, relation type, qualifier key or polarity not listed here is a violation. SYNTHETIC-friendly: ontology itself is generic and contains no case content.

researcher.description: A named human author or researcher mentioned in the text.
researcher.merge_rule: casefold(label) with whitespace collapsed; cross-paper merge allowed only with explicit merge op + reason

material.description: A chemical compound, composition or class of material.
material.merge_rule: casefold(label) with spaces/hyphens stripped; formula/name alias pairs need explicit merge op + evidence

method.description: An experimental or computational procedure, technique or protocol.

task.description: A research goal or application target (e.g. fabricating a stable solar cell).

metric.description: A measurable quantity or figure of merit.
metric.merge_rule: casefold(label); abbreviation↔full-name pairs (e.g. PCE ↔ power conversion efficiency) need explicit merge op

condition.description: A test/measurement condition (illumination, temperature, humidity, duration...).
condition.merge_rule: casefold(label) with whitespace collapsed; NEVER merge conditions with different parameter values

sample.description: A specific physical sample, device, layer or specimen. Identity is per-paper.
sample.merge_rule: NEVER auto-merge across papers; same name in two papers is a nonmerge candidate, not a merge

dataset.description: A named dataset or corpus of measurements.

claim.description: An assertion made by a paper, including numeric findings. Claims are never merged; conflicting numeric claims under different conditions stay separate nodes.
claim.merge_rule: never merge; contradictions are expressed via contradicts/compares edges
claim.example: the champion device reached PCE 21.1% under 1-sun illumination

compares.description: Two claims are compared on a metric, without a stated winner.

outperforms.description: Subject claim is strictly better than object claim on the given metric under the given condition. Direction matters.

supports.description: Subject claim provides direct evidence for object claim. Reviews/hearsay do NOT qualify; use reviews-cites instead.

contradicts.description: Subject claim conflicts with object claim under comparable conditions. Different-condition numeric differences are NOT contradictions; keep both claims and optionally link with compares.

measures.description: Subject is measured/characterized on the object metric. If a numeric value qualifier is present, metric and condition are mandatory (rule NUMERIC_REQUIRES_METRIC_CONDITION).

reports.description: A claim reports a numeric value for a metric under a condition. This is the only relation that carries a mandatory numeric value.

reviews-cites.description: Subject claim mentions/reviews/cites object claim from another paper. Citation context is required so review-hearsay is never confused with direct evidence.

aliases.description: Subject and object are the same entity under different surface forms (abbreviation, alias, case variant). Subject and object node types MUST be identical (rule SAME_TYPE_REQUIRED).

metric.description: metric label or metric node id the edge is about

condition.description: condition label or condition node id

value.description: numeric value of a measurement; triggers NUMERIC_REQUIRES_METRIC_CONDITION

unit.description: unit string, linearized as plain text (e.g. '%', 'h')

note.description: free short note; must not carry content that belongs in typed qualifiers

global_rules.description: Any edge carrying a numeric 'value' qualifier MUST also carry non-empty 'metric' (or have a metric-typed object) and 'condition' qualifiers.
For relation 'aliases', subject and object entity types must be identical.
Entity types, relation types, qualifier keys and polarities outside this ontology are rejected.
Every node/edge/merge/nonmerge/unreported item must carry evidence {source_id, paragraph_id, quote} where quote is an exact substring of the cited paragraph.

error_codes.BAD_JSON_LINE: line is not a parseable JSON object
error_codes.UNKNOWN_OP: op is not one of node/edge/merge/nonmerge/unreported/note
error_codes.BAD_SHAPE: required fields missing or wrong JSON types
error_codes.DUPLICATE_ID: node or edge id already defined in this extraction
error_codes.UNKNOWN_ENTITY_TYPE: entity type not declared in ontology
error_codes.UNKNOWN_RELATION: relation type not declared in ontology
error_codes.DOMAIN_MISMATCH: subject entity type not in relation domain
error_codes.RANGE_MISMATCH: object entity type not in relation range
error_codes.SAME_TYPE_REQUIRED: aliases edge links nodes of different entity types
error_codes.MISSING_QUALIFIER: a required qualifier key is absent or empty
error_codes.UNKNOWN_QUALIFIER: qualifier key not declared in ontology
error_codes.QUALIFIER_TYPE_MISMATCH: qualifier value has wrong JSON type (e.g. value must be a number)
error_codes.POLARITY_MISMATCH: edge declares a polarity different from the relation's fixed polarity
error_codes.UNKNOWN_NODE_REF: edge/merge references a node id that does not exist
error_codes.SELF_EDGE: edge subject and object are the same node
error_codes.ADDRESS_NOT_FOUND: source_id or paragraph_id not present in the discovered corpus
error_codes.QUOTE_NOT_SUBSTRING: quote is not an exact substring of the cited paragraph text
error_codes.REPAIR_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED: more than one repair pass attempted

repair_policy.description: Pass 1 validates the model draft. Violations go to quarantine.json with typed error codes. The model may then write ONE repair file containing corrected replacements for quarantined items (same ids). Pass 2 validates the repair; items still failing remain quarantined permanently (final=true). No third pass exists.
